docs.title: GP0001
docs.text:
Parser - unexpected token

The parser saw a token where it expected a different one. Check for missing punctuation, an unmatched delimiter, or an out-of-place keyword.

docs.title: GP0002
docs.text:
Parser - unexpected end of input

The parser reached end-of-file in the middle of a construct. Finish the expression, statement, or item - or remove it.

docs.title: GP0003
docs.text:
Parser - unterminated delimiter

A balanced construct (block, tuple, array, string literal) was left unterminated. Add the matching closing delimiter.

docs.title: GP0004
docs.text:
Parser - chained comparison without parentheses

Comparison operators like == / != / < are not associative. Parenthesise the operands: (a == b) && (b == c).

docs.title: GP0005
docs.text:
Parser - chained range operator

Range operators (.., ..=) are not associative. Parenthesise the operands: (a..b)..c.

docs.title: GP0006
docs.text:
Parser - struct literal in scrutinee

A braced struct literal in the scrutinee of if/while/match is ambiguous with the block. Wrap the literal in (...).

docs.title: GP0007
docs.text:
Parser - pipe right-hand side not callable

The right-hand side of |> must be a callable: a function reference, a method call, or a closure.

docs.title: GP0008
docs.text:
Parser - assignment outside statement position

Assignment (=, +=, …) only appears at statement position. If you need an expression, return the right-hand side directly.

docs.title: GP0009
docs.text:
Parser - expected integer literal

An integer literal is required at this position.

docs.title: GP0010
docs.text:
Parser - expected string literal

A string literal is required at this position.

docs.title: GP0011
docs.text:
Parser - invalid tuple index

A tuple index must be a plain decimal integer (p.0, p.1). Hex, binary, or octal indices are not accepted.

docs.title: GP0012
docs.text:
Parser - malformed label

A label identifier is required after the leading '.

docs.title: GP0013
docs.text:
Parser - malformed attribute

An attribute is malformed. Accepted forms are #[attr], #[attr(args)], and #[attr = value].

docs.title: GP0014
docs.text:
Parser - malformed use declaration

A use declaration could not be parsed. Check the path for stray punctuation or an unfinished brace list.

docs.title: GP0015
docs.text:
Parser - unexpected construct

Two consecutive tokens formed something the parser does not recognise.

docs.title: GP0016
docs.text:
Parser - reserved extern keyword

The extern keyword is reserved but has no source-level item form. Gossamer's FFI surface is the [rust-bindings] section of project.toml plus the gossamer-binding crate.

docs.title: GP0017
docs.text:
Parser - parser recursion limit

An expression exceeded the parser's nesting limit. Split it into smaller helpers.

docs.title: GP0018
docs.text:
Lexer - malformed token

The lexer rejected a malformed string, comment, escape, or token spelling.

docs.title: GP0019
docs.text:
Parser - statement outside entry file

Executable statements belong in the entry file or inside a function, not in a module body.

docs.title: GP0020
docs.text:
Parser - mixed entry forms

An entry file cannot combine bare top-level statements with an explicit fn main.

docs.title: GP0021
docs.text:
Parser - malformed format placeholder

A format placeholder must be a binding name, format specification, or positional placeholder.

docs.title: GP0022
docs.text:
Parser - unserializable derived field

Automatic serialization cannot be generated for a field with an unsupported type.

docs.title: GP0023
docs.text:
Parser - format argument count mismatch

The number of positional arguments must equal the number of positional placeholders.

docs.title: GP0024
docs.text:
Parser - non-literal format template

Format macros require a literal template so placeholders can be checked at compile time.

docs.title: GP0026
docs.text:
Parser - inclusive range missing upper bound

The inclusive range operator ..= requires an upper bound. Use .. for an open upper end.

docs.title: GP0027
docs.text:
Parser - $ is not part of the language

$ used to spell the slot a |> step filled. A step that needs the value in a particular slot is a closure, as in x |> |v| f(a, v); a method already chains, as in x.trim(); a callback is a closure or a function named in value position.

docs.title: GP0029
docs.text:
Parser - match arm missing arrow

Add => after the match arm pattern and optional guard.

docs.title: GP0030
docs.text:
Parser - match arm missing body

Add the expression or block produced by the match arm.

docs.title: GP0031
docs.text:
Parser - match arm missing separator

Separate same-line expression arms with a comma, or start the next arm on a new line.

docs.title: GP0032
docs.text:
Parser - removed collection literal

A bracket spelling that used to build a container is no longer syntax. Construct the container through its type: Type::new() or Type::from([a, b, c]).

docs.title: GP0033
docs.text:
Parser - text after a triple-quote opener

A multi-line """ literal carried text on the same line as its opening delimiter. The body starts on the next line, and the indentation it shares with the closing """ is stripped from every line.

docs.title: GP0034
docs.text:
Parser - missing item type

A const or static item was declared without a type annotation. These items are never inferred from their initialiser, so the type is written after the name: const EPS: f64 = 1e-12.

docs.title: GP0035
docs.text:
Parser - duplicate slice-pattern rest

A slice pattern wrote more than one ... One rest binding splits the elements into a prefix and a suffix, as in [first, ..rest, last].

docs.title: GP0036
docs.text:
Parser - duplicate struct-literal spread

A struct literal wrote more than one ..base functional update. Keep a single base value and list every overridden field explicitly.

docs.title: GP0037
docs.text:
Parser - refutable let without else

A let whose pattern can fail to match was written without an else block. Give the failure a diverging path: let Some(x) = opt else { return }.

docs.title: GP0038
docs.text:
Parser - unsupported visibility restriction

The three visibilities are private (no annotation), pub(package), and pub.

docs.title: GP0039
docs.text:
Parser - serde turbofish names an uncovered type

A codec is synthesized per concrete struct whose fields the synthesizer can classify. Exchange a concrete struct, read the document dynamically with json::parse, or hand-write the function.

docs.title: GP0040
docs.text:
Parser - hyphen in a use path

- is subtraction, never part of an identifier. A dependency's module name is its package name with each - replaced by _, so pgsql-gos is imported as use pgsql_gos.

docs.title: GP0041
docs.text:
Parser - pipe step with arguments is not a closure

A |> step that writes its own arguments leaves the piped value no slot. Write it as a closure whose parameter is that slot: x |> |v| f(a, v).

docs.title: GP0042
docs.text:
Parser - targets written as a parenthesised tuple

A binding and an assignment both list their targets without parentheses: let a, b = value and a, b = x, y. Parentheses group a pattern that sits beside others - a match arm, a for binding, a parameter, or a nested element of the list.

docs.title: GP0043
docs.text:
Parser - mod declaration ended in ;

A statement ends at its newline, and a trailing semicolon is invalid everywhere else in the language. Write mod name.

docs.title: GP0044
docs.text:
Parser - callable type written as something other than Fn

The language has one callable type, Fn(args) -> ret. There is no raw function-pointer shape and no FnMut / FnOnce distinction to draw.

docs.title: GP0045
docs.text:
Parser - argument label bound with =

Every keyed form in the language binds with : - a struct field, a map entry, a cohort header setting. Write name: value.

docs.title: GP0046
docs.text:
Parser - unsafe grants nothing

No operation is withheld outside an unsafe block or from a safe fn. The keyword stays reserved for a future raw-FFI story.

docs.title: GP0047
docs.text:
Parser - opaque alias written type X = new T

new reads as allocation to a reader arriving from any other language. Write newtype X = T.

docs.title: GP0048
docs.text:
Parser - go is retired

Every goroutine is a spawn attached to the cohort { } it is written inside, which every spawn outside main must have (GT0086). go evaluated its operands at the spawn site, so --fix hoists a computed operand into a temporary.

docs.title: GP0049
docs.text:
Parser - compiler-known call written with a !

The set of compiler-known names is closed and recognised at the (, so there is nothing a sigil disambiguates. Write println(..), format(..), matches(..).

docs.title: GP0050
docs.text:
Parser - enum representation is not an unsigned width

A discriminant is a count, so its store is unsigned. Write enum Name : u8 { .. }, with a width between 1 and 64 bits.

docs.title: GP0051
docs.text:
Parser - regex! / sql! moved into their modules

Write regex::compile("…") and sql::statement("…"). A literal argument is still validated while the program is compiled.

docs.title: GT0079
docs.text:
Types - pointer wrapper written

Every value is heap-shared and reference-counted already, so Box<T> / Rc<T> / Arc<T> name no choice the writer has to make. Write the inner type.

docs.title: GT0080
docs.text:
Types - String::parse called

The parse surface is to_i64, to_f64, and to_bool: each parses the whole string and answers an Option<T>. Add .ok_or(..) where a Result is wanted.

docs.title: GT0081
docs.text:
Types - enum representation too narrow for its variants

A declared width is exact - it is what the discriminant is stored in - so it is never widened silently. Write a width that holds every variant, or drop it.

docs.title: GT0082
docs.text:
Types - reference passed where a value is taken

A parameter that is not &mut takes the value, and a reference names one rather than being one, so the compiled tiers would hand the callee the address. Write *x.

docs.title: GT0083
docs.text:
Types - write through a value that is not a reference

* reaches the place a reference names, and a value has no such place, so the write would reach nothing. Write the binding directly, or make the parameter &mut T and pass &mut at the call site.

docs.title: GT0084
docs.text:
Types - impl of a trait the language supplies itself

Hashing, copying, release, marker safety, and the Into / TryInto / IntoIterator directions are the language's, not a per-type choice, so the block would declare a contract nothing dispatches through. The diagnostic names what the language does and what to write in its place - a From impl on the target, a defer, an inherent method - or remove the block.

docs.title: GT0085
docs.text:
Types - heap over a type that writes its own cmp

A MinHeap or MaxHeap keeps its elements in the order they went in and reads them back with no comparator to call, so an element whose type writes its own cmp would silently not be ordered by it. A sequence orders on demand and does route through the type's cmp, and a BTreeSet or BTreeMap seats its entries by it: sort a Vec<T>, use a sorted set, or key the heap on a value that carries the order.

docs.title: GT0086
docs.text:
Types - spawn outside a cohort block

A spawn must be written lexically inside a cohort { } in its own function body; main is the one exemption, since the root cohort's extent is main's own. Elsewhere the child attaches to whatever cohort the caller happens to be inside, which neither the callee's signature nor the call site says, and to the root cohort - whose extent is the process - when the program has none. Open a block around the spawns and the code that collects from them.

docs.title: GP0052
docs.text:
Parser - build-time validated call without a literal

sql::statement was handed something other than a literal. The statement is checked while the program is compiled, so it has to be there to check; a statement built at run time is an ordinary String and needs no wrapper.

docs.title: GT0087
docs.text:
Types - wrapping arithmetic written as a method

Wrapping arithmetic has one spelling, the operator: x +% y, x -% y, and x *% y wrap at the operands' declared width on every tier. x.wrapping_add(y) and x.wrapping_mul(y) are not integer methods; gos check --fix rewrites them.

docs.title: GT0088
docs.text:
Types - const generic argument not inferred

A call to a function with a const generic parameter gave it no value. A const parameter takes its value from the call: an explicit f::<4>(..) argument, or the length of an array argument whose type names it. Name the value with a turbofish.

docs.title: GT0089
docs.text:
Types - unsupported vector type or operation

A Simd or Mask vector named an element type, a lane count, or an operation the vector type does not support. Simd<T, N> takes f32, f64, i32, i64, u8, or u32 lanes and N of 2, 4, 8, or 16 (16 for u8, i32, and u32); Simd::splat takes its lane count from the annotated type.

docs.title: GT0090
docs.text:
Types - parallel adapter callback that is not provably pure

A parallel adapter runs its callback on many workers at once, so the callback must be a closure literal with a pure body or a named pure function. A callable reached through a binding is not decidable at the call site, and a closure that writes a container it captured would have every worker write the same container. Collect the results and combine them afterwards, or use cohort { } with spawn for work that performs effects.

docs.title: GT0091
docs.text:
Types - ordered range bounds not written in the call

m.range(r) on a BTreeMap reads its bounds from the range written in the call, and each bound is a key: m.range("b".."d"), m.range(lo..=hi), m.range(lo..), m.range(..hi), or m.range(..). A range stored in a binding carries no bounds a key can be compared with, so write the range in place.

docs.title: GT0092
docs.text:
Types - field read from a closure parameter of undecided type

A field was read from a closure parameter with no annotation, and the closure is never handed to anything that says what it takes, so nothing decides the parameter's type. The field's layout depends on that type: annotate the parameter, |r: http::Request| r.path, or pass the closure where its parameter type is known.

docs.title: GP0056
docs.text:
Parser - retired cohort isolation spelling

context::Context is the cancellation type a cohort may one day inherit; this setting decides whether a child gets an OS thread of its own, so it is isolation: Isolation::Shared or isolation: Isolation::Thread. --fix rewrites it.

docs.title: GP0057
docs.text:
Parser - literal regex pattern that does not compile

A string literal handed to regex::compile is not a pattern the regex engine compiles. The literal is compiled while the program is parsed, with the engine and settings regex::compile uses at run time, so the call would only ever answer Err.

docs.title: GP0058
docs.text:
Parser - malformed literal SQL statement

A string literal handed to sql::statement is not a well-formed statement: it is empty, or its parentheses do not balance. The statement is checked while the program is parsed.

docs.title: GP0059
docs.text:
Parser - range pattern bound that is not a literal

A range pattern bound is a literal, or a primitive integer limit such as i64::MIN or u8::MAX, which stands for its literal. Any other path - a const, a static, an enum variant - is not a bound: match it with a guard instead (n if n >= LOW => ..).

docs.title: GP0053
docs.text:
Parser - Display rendering declared as to_string

Both rendering contracts declare one method that answers a String, so both are written fn fmt; the impl header is what decides which channel a value reaches, {} taking Display and {:?} taking Debug. x.to_string() still renders through Display.

docs.title: GP0054
docs.text:
Parser - shared reference in parameter position

An argument is passed without copying whatever its type, and a callee cannot write to the caller's variable unless the parameter says &mut, so f(m: &Map) and f(m: Map) have the same cost and the same guarantee. A sequence view is written [T], and &mut [T] is the form that writes through. --fix drops the &.

docs.title: GP0055
docs.text:
Parser - shared reference on a call argument

No parameter is a shared reference, so the sigil changes nothing: an argument is passed without copying either way, and a callee writes to the caller's variable only through a &mut parameter, which is spelled &mut at the call too. --fix drops the &.

docs.title: GR0001
docs.text:
Resolve - unresolved name

A name used in source could not be resolved to a declaration. Check the spelling, whether a use brings the name into scope, and whether the item is visible at this location.

docs.title: GR0002
docs.text:
Resolve - wrong namespace

A name was resolved to the wrong namespace (value vs. type). Check the declaration and the spelling.

docs.title: GR0003
docs.text:
Resolve - duplicate item

Two items in the same module share a name. Rename one of them or move it into a distinct mod.

docs.title: GR0004
docs.text:
Resolve - duplicate import

The same path was imported twice in the same use list. Drop the duplicate.

docs.title: GR0005
docs.text:
Resolve - unknown module path

The use names a std:: module path that does not exist. Every module has exactly one canonical path (e.g. JSON lives at std::encoding::json); check gos doc or the stdlib reference for the module's path.

docs.title: GR0006
docs.text:
Resolve - removed stdlib item

A container spelling that a canonical name replaced. Each container has exactly one name - import and write that one.

docs.title: GR0007
docs.text:
Resolve - unknown stdlib item

The use names a module that exists but an item that module does not export. Check the item spelling; gos doc std::<module> lists every name a module exports.

docs.title: GR0017
docs.text:
Resolver - break or continue with no loop

A break or continue has no loop to act on: either none encloses it, or the label it names is not carried by any enclosing loop. A closure body is a separate function, so a loop outside it is not a target.

docs.title: GR0018
docs.text:
Resolver - compiler-known call named as a value path

A path named one of the compiler-known calls - println, format, panic, and the rest of the fixed set. Each expands where it is written and the runtime binds no callable for it, so the path has nothing to call or pass as a value. Write it as name(..); it needs no import.

docs.title: GR0019
docs.text:
Resolver - two dependency packages under one module name

Two dependency packages are reached under one module name. A - is not part of an identifier, so a package name carrying one is reached from source as the same name with _ in its place, which two packages can share. Give one of them a name of its own in [dependencies], or import each through use "id" as name.

docs.title: GR0020
docs.text:
Resolver - declaration under a compiler-known call name

A fn or a binding was declared under one of the compiler-known call names - println, format, matches, and the rest of the fixed set. Each expands where it is written, so the declaration could never be reached. Give it a name of its own.

docs.title: GR0021
docs.text:
Resolve - std free call written data-last

A std free function was called with its data argument in the slot it occupied before every module took its data first. The call still means what it did, so nothing else in the body is affected; write the data argument first, which is what makes iter::map(xs, f) read as the xs.map(f) it stands for.

docs.title: GT0001
docs.text:
Types - type mismatch

The type checker could not reconcile two types it expected to match. The primary label shows the location of the mismatch; the note: line names the conflicting types.

docs.title: GT0002
docs.text:
Types - unresolved method

The type checker could not find a method with the supplied name on the receiver type. Check for a typo, a missing use, or a trait impl that lives in an unreachable module.

docs.title: GT0003
docs.text:
Types - unresolved operator

The operator is not defined for the operand types. Check the operand types and use the correct operator.

docs.title: GT0004
docs.text:
Match exhaustiveness - non-exhaustive match

A match expression does not cover every possible value. Add an arm for the pattern(s) listed under help:.

docs.title: GT0005
docs.text:
Types - non-primitive cast

The as cast is restricted to a whitelist: numeric ↔ numeric, bool/char → integer, u8 → char, and same-type no-ops. Struct / enum / String sources are rejected. Use a conversion method when you need serialisation; as does not run code.

docs.title: GT0044
docs.text:
Types - generic return type not inferred

A generic return payload cannot be inferred from call arguments alone. Add an explicit generic argument or assign the expression to an expected Result type.

docs.title: GT0045
docs.text:
Types - question mark not supported here

The ? operator can only unwrap Result inside a Result-returning function or Option inside an Option-returning function.

docs.title: Lints
docs.text:
The Gossamer linter ships 53 day-one checks. Each has a short identifier suitable for #[lint(allow(...))] and a long-form explanation available via gos lint --explain <id>. This page is auto-generated from gossamer-lint; hand edits are overwritten on the next run of cargo xtask docs-lints.

Code Identifier Default GL0001 unused_variable warn GL0002 unused_import warn GL0003 unused_mut_variable warn GL0004 needless_return warn GL0005 needless_bool warn GL0006 comparison_to_bool_literal warn GL0007 single_match warn GL0008 shadowed_binding warn GL0009 unchecked_result warn GL0010 empty_block warn GL0011 panic_in_main warn GL0012 redundant_clone warn GL0013 double_negation warn GL0014 self_assignment warn GL0015 todo_macro warn GL0054 i64_only_container_family warn GL0056 no_effect_statement warn GL0016 bool_literal_in_condition warn GL0017 let_and_return warn GL0018 collapsible_if warn GL0019 if_same_then_else warn GL0021 needless_else_after_return warn GL0022 self_compare warn GL0023 identity_op warn GL0024 unit_let warn GL0025 float_eq_zero warn GL0026 empty_else warn GL0027 match_bool warn GL0028 needless_parens warn GL0029 manual_not_equal warn GL0030 nested_ternary_if warn GL0031 absurd_range warn GL0032 string_literal_concat warn GL0033 chained_negation_literals warn GL0034 if_not_else warn GL0035 empty_string_concat warn GL0036 println_newline_only warn GL0037 match_same_arms warn GL0038 manual_swap warn GL0039 consecutive_assignment warn GL0040 large_unreadable_literal warn GL0041 redundant_closure warn GL0042 empty_if_body warn GL0043 bool_to_int_match warn GL0044 fn_returns_unit_explicit warn GL0045 let_with_unit_type warn GL0046 useless_default_only_match warn GL0047 unnecessary_parens_in_condition warn GL0048 pattern_matching_unit warn GL0049 panic_without_message warn GL0050 empty_loop warn GL0051 fill_loop warn GL0052 substring_byte_scan warn

docs.title: unused_variable
docs.text: Declares a let binding whose name is never read. Prefix the name with _ to silence explicitly (e.g. _tmp) when the binding is intentional but unused.

docs.title: unused_import
docs.text: A use declaration whose imported name is never referenced. Remove the import or reference the name in the file.

docs.title: unused_mut_variable
docs.text: A binding marked mut that is never reassigned. Drop the mut keyword.

docs.title: needless_return
docs.text: return expr at the tail of a block is the same as writing expr by itself. Prefer the tail form for symmetry with the rest of the expression language.

docs.title: needless_bool
docs.text: if cond { true } else { false } is the same as cond. The inverted form is !cond.

docs.title: comparison_to_bool_literal
docs.text: x == true reads worse than x, and x == false reads worse than !x. Drop the literal.

docs.title: single_match
docs.text: A match with a single arm reads better as if let PATTERN = .... Single-arm match is almost always a half-written exhaustive match.

docs.title: shadowed_binding
docs.text: A let binding in the same block shadows an earlier one. Rename one of them to make the data flow obvious.

docs.title: unchecked_result
docs.text: let _ = expr? silently discards an error. Either handle the Err branch explicitly or propagate with ? so the caller sees it.

docs.title: empty_block
docs.text: An empty {} block is almost always a mistake. Add an explicit () tail if the block is intentional.

docs.title: panic_in_main
docs.text: panic! inside main aborts without a clean exit code. Return a Result from main and use ? so the error propagates.

docs.title: redundant_clone
docs.text: Calling .clone() on a literal or already-copied value is redundant. Drop the call.

docs.title: double_negation
docs.text: !!x collapses to x when x: bool. If the double negation is intentional for truthiness coercion, use an explicit cast.

docs.title: self_assignment
docs.text: Assigning a variable to itself does nothing. The statement is usually the residue of a refactor - remove it.

docs.title: todo_macro
docs.text: todo() and unimplemented() are placeholders, not shippable expressions. Implement the branch before merging.

docs.title: i64_only_container_family
docs.text: std::collections::{queue,stack,deque,heap,ordered_*} hold i64 only and return a new container from every mutator, which duplicates Queue, Stack, Deque, MinHeap, BTreeSet, and BTreeMap at a narrower element type. Deliberately not auto-fixable: the two families differ in more than spelling. peek answers 0 on an empty container where the type answers None, so a mechanical rewrite would keep type-checking and change what an empty container means.

docs.title: no_effect_statement
docs.text: An expression statement that only computes - a path, a literal, arithmetic over them - and hands its value to nothing. A newline followed by -, *, or & starts a NEW statement, so a continuation meant as part of the line above becomes one of these. Join it to that line (end the previous line with the operator, or parenthesise), or bind what it computes. A builtin method that answers a new value and writes nothing - v.dedup(), s.trim(), s.to_uppercase() - is reported the same way when its result is dropped: the receiver is unchanged, so bind the result (v = v.dedup()).

docs.title: bool_literal_in_condition
docs.text: if true { ... } / while false { ... } - the branch is decided at compile time. Drop the control-flow construct.

docs.title: let_and_return
docs.text: let x = expr; x at the tail of a block is just expr. Drop the needless binding.

docs.title: collapsible_if
docs.text: if a { if b { ... } } can be combined into if a && b { ... }. Easier to scan.

docs.title: if_same_then_else
docs.text: Both branches of the if are identical. Drop the branch and keep the body once.

docs.title: needless_else_after_return
docs.text: if cond { return X } else { Y } - the else is unreachable fall-through. Un-nest the else body.

docs.title: self_compare
docs.text: Comparing a value to itself is always true (for ==, <=, >=) or false (for !=, <, >). Use the constant.

docs.title: identity_op
docs.text: x + 0, x - 0, x * 1, x / 1 all equal x. The operation adds nothing but noise.

docs.title: unit_let
docs.text: let x = () binds the unit value, which is almost never useful. Drop the let.

docs.title: float_eq_zero
docs.text: Equality against a float literal is almost never what you want - floating-point arithmetic rarely produces the exact bit pattern. Compare (x - y).abs() < eps with an explicit tolerance.

docs.title: empty_else
docs.text: else {} adds no information. Drop the else and let the if stand alone.

docs.title: match_bool
docs.text: match b { true => ... false => ... } is an if in disguise. Rewrite as if b { ... } else { ... }.

docs.title: needless_parens
docs.text: (x) without a trailing comma is a needless pair of parens - x reads the same. (x,) is a one-tuple and means something different. Closure parameters follow the same rule: write |t|, not |(t)|.

docs.title: manual_not_equal
docs.text: !(a == b) is just a != b. Prefer the direct operator.

docs.title: nested_ternary_if
docs.text: Three or more if / else if layers that all test one value against a pattern are a match written the long way. Rewrite them as match on that value. A chain whose arms test unrelated conditions, or compare with < and >, is left alone: match would only move those into guards.

docs.title: absurd_range
docs.text: A literal range whose lower bound exceeds its upper bound is empty. Swap the bounds or double-check the intent.

docs.title: string_literal_concat
docs.text: "a" + "b" can be written directly as "ab". Let the source reflect the final value.

docs.title: chained_negation_literals
docs.text: -(-x) is x. The extra unary does nothing.

docs.title: if_not_else
docs.text: if !cond { A } else { B } scans better as if cond { B } else { A }. Flip the branches and drop the !.

docs.title: empty_string_concat
docs.text: Concatenating an empty string literal is a no-op. Drop the "" + or + "".

docs.title: println_newline_only
docs.text: println("") already writes a newline. Don't pass "\n" and don't call it twice to emit a blank line.

docs.title: match_same_arms
docs.text: Two match arms share the same body. Either collapse them with | alternation or extract the shared body into a helper.

docs.title: manual_swap
docs.text: Three consecutive statements let tmp = a; a = b; b = tmp swap two bindings via a temporary. Prefer a destructuring assignment once the language supports it, or at minimum document why the swap is needed.

docs.title: consecutive_assignment
docs.text: Two back-to-back assignments to the same place - the earlier value is dead before it's read. Drop the first or consolidate the logic into one statement.

docs.title: large_unreadable_literal
docs.text: Integer literals of five or more digits are easier to scan with _ as thousands separators: 1_000_000 instead of 1000000.

docs.title: redundant_closure
docs.text: |x| f(x) is a closure that just forwards to f. Pass f directly.

docs.title: empty_if_body
docs.text: An if cond { } else { body } is the same as if !cond { body }. Invert the condition and drop the empty branch.

docs.title: bool_to_int_match
docs.text: match b { true => 1, false => 0 } is an if in disguise that happens to return an integer. Prefer if b { 1 } else { 0 }.

docs.title: fn_returns_unit_explicit
docs.text: fn f() -> () { ... } is the same as fn f() { ... }. The explicit -> () is noise.

docs.title: let_with_unit_type
docs.text: let _: () = expr annotates the binding with the unit type. If expr was going to return () anyway, the annotation is noise. If it wasn't, the annotation forces a coercion - use a plain statement instead.

docs.title: useless_default_only_match
docs.text: match x { _ => expr } always runs expr - the match adds nothing. Drop the match (and add let _ = x if evaluating the scrutinee has side effects).

docs.title: unnecessary_parens_in_condition
docs.text: if (cond) { ... } wraps the condition in a single-tuple expression. Drop the parens: if cond { ... }.

docs.title: pattern_matching_unit
docs.text: match () { ... } has exactly one reachable arm. Drop the match and run the body directly.

docs.title: panic_without_message
docs.text: panic() with no argument leaves the post-mortem with nothing to render. Always pass a brief explanation.

docs.title: empty_loop
docs.text: loop {} with no body busy-waits forever at 100% CPU. Add a break, a continue, or replace with a real wait primitive.

docs.title: fill_loop
docs.text: A for _ in 0..n { xs.push(value) } loop that pushes the same literal every iteration is the repeat literal spelled long: let xs = [value; n] builds the identical vec in one expression (byte-packed for bool / u8 elements).

docs.title: substring_byte_scan
docs.text: s.substring(i, i + 1) allocates a String per step of a scan. substring takes byte offsets, so s.byte_at(i) reads the same position directly as an i64: compare with byte literals (s.byte_at(i) >= b'0'), do arithmetic on it (s.byte_at(i) - b'0'), and render with s.byte_at(i) as char. s[i] is not that byte: indexing counts Unicode scalars, so it yields the char at character index i.

docs.title: Building with Zig
docs.text: Zig is optional. Gossamer never requires it. It is a convenient, self-contained C toolchain that helps in a few cross-compilation and static-linking cases - most usefully cross-compiling to a different architecture's musl target. This page explains when it helps, how to use it, what it replaces, and how narrowly Gossamer itself relies on it.

docs.title: What a native build actually needs
docs.text:
gos build and gos build --release differ in the external tools they call:

Command Backend External tools gos build Cranelift AOT A C linker only (cc / $CC / ld.lld) gos build --release LLVM -O3 llc + opt (LLVM 18 and newer; 22 preferred), via PATH or GOS_LLC / GOS_LLVM_OPT

The gos binary links no libLLVM - it shells out to llc / opt - so the toolchain itself is portable regardless of how you build your own programs. Two consequences follow:

  • Zig does not replace LLVM. gos build --release needs a real llc / opt. Zig bundles clang but not standalone llc / opt, so it cannot stand in for the --release codegen tools.
  • Zig can serve as the linker / C driver. Where a build needs a C compiler or a libc sysroot - final linking, or building C dependencies such as mimalloc, ring, and zstd - zig cc supplies both from a single self-contained download.

docs.title: Using zig
docs.text:
The simplest path is cargo-zigbuild, which wraps zig cc as the C compiler and linker:

cargo install cargo-zigbuild        # once; also needs `zig` on PATH
cargo zigbuild --release --target aarch64-unknown-linux-musl --bin gos

Or point Cargo at zig as the C compiler for a specific target directly:

rustup target add x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
CC_x86_64_unknown_linux_musl="zig cc -target x86_64-linux-musl" \
  cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl --bin gos

Zig is a single extractable archive with no system installation, which is what makes it convenient in a CI job or a clean container.

docs.title: You usually do not need it
docs.text:
For native builds zig is never required:

  • Native static musl x86_64. rustup target add x86_64-unknown-linux-musl plus musl-tools (which provides musl-gcc) is enough - Gossamer is pure Rust plus a few C dependencies, with no cross-architecture sysroot problem on the native target. This is how the static gos-<version>-linux-x86_64-musl release binary is produced.
  • gos build (Cranelift). Only a host cc.
  • gos build --release (LLVM). llc / opt from a system LLVM, or pointed at with GOS_LLC / GOS_LLVM_OPT.

LLVM 18 and newer build the same program. The emitter writes IR every one of those majors parses, and every fixture produces bit-identical output across them, so any of them is a supported build.

The version this toolchain prefers is the major rustc bundles, which is LLVM 22, and an older major is accepted with a one-line warning naming what it gives up: cross-language optimisation with the Rust runtime, which needs the majors to match. That is a difference in optimisation, not in whether the build works. Most distributions stop a major or two short, so 22 usually comes from apt.llvm.org on Linux (wget -qO- \ https://apt.llvm.org/llvm.sh | sudo bash -s -- 22) or from brew install llvm@22 on macOS.

docs.title: Why Gossamer uses zig, and how narrowly
docs.text:
In this repository zig appears in exactly one place: cross-compiling the static-musl aarch64 runtime archive in the release workflow. Bare clang --target=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl has no musl sysroot and fails to find string.h; zig ships a bundled musl sysroot plus a working cross C compiler, so the aarch64 static-musl libgossamer_runtime.a builds cleanly from an x86 CI host as a single self-contained download.

It was chosen for convenience, not necessity, and it is replaceable:

  • A real musl cross toolchain (musl-cross / aarch64-linux-musl-gcc).
  • The cross tool (Docker-based cross builds).
  • For the native x86_64 static-musl binary, nothing extra at all - rustup's musl target plus musl-tools.

Zig earns its keep only for the cross-architecture (aarch64-from-x86) musl case. It is not a Gossamer dependency, not part of gos, and never required to build your own programs.
